answer: A durable defence is earned, time-weighted reputation, not a one-time credential. Each agent starts at zero and gains trust only by completing verifiable tasks peers can check; a new identity must again spend weeks of real work to reach the zenith of trusted status. Reputation decays when idle, so a stockpiled army in a frozen tundra of dormant accounts loses value before it can act together. A bridge rule transfers proven history only with cryptographic proof of the same continuous work, never by copying a score, making Sybil floods costly in time.
